question: What is the primary purpose of conducting a systematic physical examination in nursing?

options.A: To replace the need for taking a patient health history
options.B: To gather objective data and establish a baseline health status
options.C: To diagnose medical conditions independently without a doctor
options.D: To minimize the time spent interacting with hospitalized patients

explanation: The primary purpose of a physical examination is to collect objective clinical data, establish baseline health measurements, and identify potential health issues to guide care. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following describes the type of data primarily gathered during a physical examination?

options.A: Subjective data reported directly by family members
options.B: Objective data observed and measured by the nurse
options.C: Historical data retrieved from previous admissions
options.D: Theoretical data gathered from nursing textbooks

explanation: Physical examinations yield objective data through the nurse's direct observation, measurement, and sensory evaluation. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is adequate lighting essential during a physical examination?

options.A: To keep the room warm for the patient
options.B: To accurately observe skin color and subtle abnormalities
options.C: To ensure heart and breath sounds can be heard clearly
options.D: To allow the patient to read educational pamphlets

explanation: Proper lighting is critical for the visual inspection component, allowing the nurse to accurately identify skin changes, rashes, and physical lesions. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which action best demonstrates psychological preparation of the patient before an exam?

options.A: Beginning the assessment immediately without speaking to avoid wasting time
options.B: Explaining the procedures clearly and obtaining informed consent
options.C: Asking family members to leave the room permanently
options.D: Dimming all the lights to help the patient fall asleep

explanation: Explaining procedures and securing consent reduces anxiety, fosters trust, and prepares the patient psychologically for the examination. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is considered the single most effective measure to prevent the spread of infections during clinical practice?

options.A: Wearing sterile gowns during every patient interaction
options.C: Using disposable stethoscopes for every patient
options.D: Administering prophylactic antibiotics to all patients

explanation: Hand hygiene is universally recognized as the single most effective way to prevent healthcare-associated infections. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h3)

question: When should gloves be worn during a physical examination according to standard precautions?

options.A: Only when the patient is known to have a communicable disease
options.B: Whenever touching non-intact skin, mucous membranes, or body fluids
options.C: Throughout the entire duration of every bed bath and physical exam
options.D: Only when drawing blood samples in the laboratory

explanation: Gloves are required whenever there is a risk of contact with blood, body fluids, mucous membranes, or non-intact skin. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the correct sequence of physical assessment techniques for a standard abdominal examination?
explanation: For the abdomen, auscultation is performed immediately after inspection so that bowel sounds are not altered by the manipulation of palpation or percussion. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of the percussion technique during a physical examination?

options.A: To measure the exact blood pressure of the patient
options.B: To determine the density, size, and borders of underlying organs
options.C: To listen to heart murmur frequencies and lung wheezes
options.D: To assess skin temperature and moisture levels

explanation: Percussion produces sound waves that help the nurse assess the underlying tissue density, organ boundaries, and whether tissues are air-filled, fluid-filled, or solid. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h4)

question: When does the general survey of a patient officially begin during a clinical encounter?

options.A: Only after the patient's vital signs have been fully recorded
options.C: The exact moment the nurse first encounters and observes the patient
options.D: When the patient is placed in a supine position on the examination couch

explanation: The general survey begins immediately upon first meeting the patient, observing overall appearance, behavior, and posture before formal hands-on assessment. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which of the following parameters is traditionally referred to as the 'fifth vital sign' in clinical practice?
explanation: Pain is routinely evaluated alongside temperature, pulse, respiration, and blood pressure, earning it the designation of the fifth vital sign. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h5)

question: During a respiratory physical assessment, which adventitious breath sound is commonly auscultated?
explanation: Crackles and wheezes are common adventitious breath sounds evaluated during lung auscultation in a respiratory assessment. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is evaluated during the musculoskeletal system physical examination?

options.A: Cranial nerve reflexes and cognitive function
options.B: Heart valve closure sounds and cardiac output
options.C: Joint range of motion, muscle strength, and spinal alignment
options.D: Bowel motility and abdominal organ size

explanation: The musculoskeletal examination specifically focuses on evaluating joint mobility, muscle strength, posture, and spinal alignment. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following represents an example of objective, professional documentation following a physical examination?

options.A: Patient is lazy and refuses to cooperate with the nursing staff.
options.B: Patient states they feel fine, but looks terrible and sickly.
options.C: Patient ambulates with an unsteady gait and has a BP of 130/80 mmHg.
options.D: Patient is obviously depressed because nobody visited them today.

explanation: Professional documentation relies on clear, factual, and measurable objective data rather than subjective opinions or judgmental language. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of verbal reporting during nursing shift handovers?

options.A: To fulfill legal requirements without updating the written patient chart
options.B: To ensure continuity of care and communicate critical patient findings
options.C: To discuss personal opinions about patient behaviors
options.D: To replace the need for conducting physical assessments on subsequent shifts

explanation: Verbal reporting during handovers ensures seamless continuity of care and alerts incoming staff to urgent or critical changes in patient status. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h7)
